rulers.note: 23 December 1253 to 26 August 1278, killed at the Marchfeld.

rulers.name: Wenceslaus II (Václav II)
rulers.note: To 21 June 1305; regencies of Kunigunda Rostislavna and Otto V of Brandenburg preceded his own rule.

rulers.name: Wenceslaus III (Václav III)
rulers.note: To 4 August 1306, murdered at Olomouc; the last Přemyslid.

rulers.name: Anna Přemyslovna with Henry of Carinthia
rulers.title: claimant queen and her husband
rulers.note: List page: Anna 4 August 1306 to 3 December 1310 (garbled row); Henry's own dates are not given. Elisabeth Richeza and Rudolf of Habsburg claimed from 1306 to 3/4 July 1307 (Rudolf died at Horažďovice). The John page: Czech forces deposed Henry of Gorizia on 3 December 1310.

rulers.name: John the Blind (John of Luxembourg)
rulers.note: 3 December 1310 to 26 August 1346 (Crécy); crowned with Elisabeth Přemyslovna 7 February 1311.

rulers.name: Charles IV (Karel IV)
rulers.note: Also Holy Roman Emperor; crowned emperor 1355.

rulers.name: Wenceslaus IV (Václav IV)
rulers.note: Deposed as King of the Romans in 1400; died 16 August 1419.

rulers.name: Sigismund (Zikmund)
rulers.note: List page: 'Effectively ruled only 1436-1437, due to the Hussite Revolution'; accepted the Compacts at Jihlava on 5 July 1436 (Hussite Wars page).

rulers.name: Albert (Albrecht Habsburský)
rulers.note: Elected by the estates in 1437 (Kingdom page); the List page names him 'Albert'. An interregnum follows, 1440 to 1453 on the List page.

rulers.name: Ladislaus the Posthumous (Ladislav Pohrobek)
rulers.note: Son of Albert; also King of Hungary; died of leukemia 1457.

rulers.name: George of Poděbrady (Jiří z Poděbrad)
rulers.note: Non-dynastic, elected by the estates in 1458; of the Czech noble House of Kunštát.

rulers.name: Vladislaus II Jagiellon (Vladislav II. Jagellonský)
rulers.note: Elected by the Diet after George's death in 1471; also King of Hungary after 1490. Matthias Corvinus was anti-king 1469-1490, never crowned, and held Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia.

rulers.name: Louis Jagiellon (Ludvík Jagellonský)
rulers.note: Also King of Hungary; killed at Mohács in 1526.

rulers.name: Ferdinand I
rulers.note: Elected king 1526; reigned to 1564 (List page). This dossier ends in 1526 when the Habsburg Monarchy takes the land.

Frederick VI of Nuremberg 'was granted hereditary control over Brandenburg in 1411' (allegiance of the estates at Tangermünde on 20 March 1414; 'officially recognized as Margrave and Prince-elector' in 1415). Jobst, who held it in pawn, died on 18 January 1411. Repair pass 2026-10-31: the 1402 pawn of the New March to the Teutonic Knights (Brandenburg page: 'the Luxembourgs pawned the region to the Teutonic Knights') is not a Bohemian loss: Brandenburg is vassal land here and the loss is margraviate-of-brandenburg's own (its 1402 loss to teutonic-order, mirrored by teutonic-order's gain); the earlier Bohemian 'loss' event was deleted as a duplicate (reviewer finding).

1419: Moravia is held by the King of Bohemia himself. Jobst page: Sigismund succeeded Jobst as margrave in 1411 (Jobst's last day was 18 January 1411); Margraviate page table: 'Sigismund | 1419-1423, son of Emperor Charles IV' with no entry for 1411-1419; List of Bohemian monarchs: Wenceslaus IV '1378-1419', Sigismund '1419-1437'. Sigismund was margrave under his brother Wenceslaus IV until 1419 and margrave and king together from 1419, so the vassal tint ends then; no page says Moravia 'returned to the king' in 1411. Albert V of Austria is margrave from 1423 to 1439 (Margraviate page table); whether that is again a fief of the Bohemian king is not on the pages, so Moravia stays direct land. Repair pass 2026-10-31: moved from 1415 (a bridge to Cliopatria) and raised from confidence 1 (reviewer thin finding).

1437: the Habsburgs take the Bohemian crown. 'When Sigismund died in 1437, the Bohemian estates elected Albert of Austria' (List page: Albert 1437-1439, then an interregnum 1440-1453). Same state, same colour.

1445: Brandenburg acquires Cottbus from Bohemia. Cottbus page: 'In 1445 Cottbus was acquired by the Margraviate of Brandenburg from Bohemia'; its affiliations list gives 'Bohemian Crown 1367-1445' and 'Margraviate of Brandenburg 1445-1618' (Lower Lusatia reached the Crown in 1367). The 20 km radius is the one electorate-of-brandenburg uses for its 1445 gain, which cites the same page; Cliopatria's Bohemia outlines hold 4 cells (about 1,012 km2) of that disc in 1415-1470 and 1492-1526. Repair pass 2026-10-31: added because the mirror loss was missing (reviewer finding).

1458: the estates elect George of Poděbrady, a Bohemian nobleman. 'After Ladislaus died of leukemia in 1457, the following year the Bohemian estates elected George of Poděbrady as king' (List page: non-dynastic, of the House of Kunštát). Same state, same colour.

region.text: Moravia, Silesia and the Lusatias, seized by Matthias

ledger.note: 1468: Matthias Corvinus invades. 'In 1468, Matthias began a war in Bohemia'; 'Matthias seized Moravia and Silesia from George'; he was elected King of Bohemia at Olomouc on 3 May 1469 (Matthias page) and 'Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia soon accepted his rule'. The Moravia dossier dates the occupation 1469; the year of the first seizure is not given.

1471: the Jagiellons take the Bohemian crown. 'George of Poděbrady died in 1471' and 'the Bohemian Diet elected the Polish prince Vladislaus of the Jagiellonian dynasty as king'. Same state, same colour.

21 July 1478: Matthias and Vladislaus ratify the peace at Olomouc. 'They solemnly ratified the peace treaty at their meeting in Olomouc on 21 July 1478'; the Kingdom, Lands and List pages date the Peace of Olomouc 1479 ('In 1479, both kings signed the Treaty of Olomouc').

region.text: Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia, held by Matthias

ledger.note: 21 July 1478: Matthias keeps Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia. 'Vladislaus ruled in Bohemia proper and Matthias in Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia.' Cliopatria draws the loss from 1475.

region.text: the crown lands: Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia

ledger.note: 1490: Matthias dies and Vladislaus takes back the crown lands. 'After Matthias died in 1490, Vladislas ruled the Bohemian crown lands' and Hungary in personal union; the Matthias page dates his death 6 April 1490. Cliopatria restores the full outline only in 1492.

region.text: Bohemia and the incorporated Crown lands pass to Ferdinand I and the Habsburg Monarchy

ledger.note: 1526: the Bohemian Diet elects Ferdinand of Habsburg and Bohemia passes to the Habsburg Monarchy. 'In 1526, Vladislaus's son, King Louis II of Hungary, was killed at the Battle of Mohács' and 'The Bohemian Diet elected Louis' brother-in-law, Archduke Ferdinand, as the new king of Bohemia'; the infobox gives Ferdinand I 16 December 1526. The kingdom lasted as a crown land to 1918.

wars.name: Ottokar II and Béla IV of Hungary over Styria (Kressenbrunn)

zones.text: Styria, ceded by Béla IV after Kressenbrunn

wars.outcome: Ottokar defeated Béla IV at Kressenbrunn in July 1260 and 'Béla now ceded Styria back to Ottokar'.
wars.note: The page does not name the Peace of Ofen or give the cession a separate date.

wars.name: Ottokar II against Rudolf of Habsburg (to the Battle on the Marchfeld)
wars.outcome: Rudolf was chosen king in 1273, placed Ottokar under the Imperial ban in 1275 and forced the November 1276 treaty giving up Austria and the neighbouring duchies; Ottokar was defeated and killed at the Marchfeld on 26 August 1278.
wars.note: Ottokar allied with Bavaria, Brandenburg and Poland in 1278. The 1274 Nuremberg decree on alienated imperial lands would also have cost him the Egerland.

wars.name: Bohemian rule in Poland, 1300-1306 (Wenceslaus II and III against Władysław the Elbow-high)

zones.text: Greater Poland, Kujavia and the Duchy of Kraków

wars.outcome: Wenceslaus II occupied Greater Poland and Kujavia in early 1300 and was crowned at Gniezno on 25 July 1300; Władysław Łokietek captured Kraków in early 1306 and Wenceslaus III was murdered on 4 August 1306 before he could invade. Repair pass 2026-10-31: Władysław I page: he mastered Sieradz-Łęczyca and Brześć Kujawski by the end of 1305 and entered Kraków on 1 September 1306; Henry III of Głogów took Greater Poland in 1306 (Henry III page).
wars.note: The Wenceslaus II page names no war; the title is descriptive.

wars.name: Wenceslaus III's claim to Hungary
wars.outcome: Wenceslaus III was crowned at Székesfehérvár on 27 August 1301 but 'the Kingdom of Hungary was split into several de facto principalities'; his father took him home in August 1304 and he handed the Holy Crown to Otto of Bavaria at Brno on 9 October 1305.
wars.note: No territory is recorded for Bohemia: the pages place no Bohemian rule inside Hungary or Slovakia.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332)
wars.outcome: John 'backed the Teutonic Knights'; the page gives no outcome for the war itself. The Silesian dukes' homage (1327, 1329) and the annexation of Głogów (1331) fall in the same years.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; the page gives John's side only.

wars.name: Bohemian-Polish dispute over Silesia and the Polish crown (to the Treaty of Trentschin)
wars.outcome: The Silesian dukes became John's vassals 1327-1342; at Trentschin on 24 August 1335 John waived the Polish crown and Casimir III renounced Silesia in perpetuity, reaffirmed by the Treaty of Namslau in 1348.
wars.note: The Treaty page names no fighting; the title is descriptive.

wars.name: Hussite Wars
wars.outcome: Crusades in 1420, 1421, 1422, 1427 and 1431 failed; after Pankrác (1 November 1420) 'almost all Bohemia fell into the hands of the Hussites'; the Taborites were beaten at Lipany on 30 May 1434 and Sigismund signed the Compacts at Jihlava on 5 July 1436.
wars.note: No border moved. The Hussite regime held the land against Sigismund's claim, which Cliopatria draws as a personal union with Hungary 1422-1439; a rebel dossier for it is not written here (see notes).

wars.name: Bohemian-Hungarian War (1468-1478)
wars.outcome: Matthias 'conquered Moravia, Silesia, and Lusatia, but he could not occupy Bohemia proper'; 'In 1478, the war ended following the treaties of Brno and the Olomouc' (peace ratified 21 July 1478); Matthias kept the three lands until his death in 1490.
wars.note: The war page pits Bohemia against 'Matthias Corvinus and Frederick III of Habsburg'. It gives no months.

certainty.note: None of the pages describes a boundary; the Bohemian mountain ring, the Austrian and Styrian acquisitions of 1251-1276 and the Polish claims of 1291-1306 are all approximate.

The Silesian-Polish frontier is sharp after the Treaty of Trentschin (24 August 1335): 'a border that remained stable and in effect until after World War I'. Every other frontier, including the Lusatian and Moravian edges, stays soft. Treaty of Trentschin page, re-read 2026-10-31: the Polish king's representatives 'in perpetuity, renounced all claims to Silesia in favour of Bohemia' and John and Charles 'finally waived their claims to the Polish throne'; the treaty moved no land, so it is not a ledger gain.
